name: explain
description: Ask the learner to EXPLAIN something in his own words — a graded check with NO options: he types a free-text answer. Unlike ask_user_question (no right answer), explain always has one. THE COMMITMENT RULE: correctAnswer is the FULL correct answer in your own words, reasoning included, COMMITTED before he ever sees the question. When his answer returns, grade it strictly against the commitment — never revise it after seeing his words. He sees the committed answer on submit. Set `nodeId` (required) to the plan node this question is about — validated at call time against the session's plan map. ONE question per turn: call a single explain, then end your turn — his answer determines the next.

type.description: REQUIRED — the question's role in the teaching cycle, as a bare word (no quotes): predict = posed BEFORE you teach the step (its own turn; the learner answers, then your teaching resolves it — arrives open, never collapsed); check = posed AFTER the step's teaching is complete (arrives collapsed behind the Check your understanding reveal). ONE question per turn either way.

nodeId.description: REQUIRED plan-tree node id this question is about — must EXACTLY match one of this session's plan_init node slugs (validated at call time; a mismatched id is rejected back to you). The lesson's position on the map derives from these tags (the node the latest tagged question is about is where the map stands; earlier ones count as visited). A node takes as many questions as it deserves: stay on one node for as many turns as the understanding needs — one reasoning step at a time, never rush forward. For off-map checks use ask_user_question.

question.description: The single question to ask. ONE question per turn: ask, then end your turn — the answer determines the next.

correctAnswer.description: REQUIRED. The full correct answer in your own words, reasoning included — COMMITTED before the learner ever sees the question. The commitment is immutable: when his answer returns, grade it strictly against this text — never revise the commitment after seeing his words, and never mark a wrong answer right to be kind. It is shown to him on submit; your next reply grades the nuance of what he wrote.

details.description: Optional extra context or instructions shown under the question.

name: ask_user_question
description: Ask the learner a single question and pause until they answer. NOT graded — there is no correct answer. Use when requirements are ambiguous, preferences are needed, a decision would materially affect the lesson, or you need an open-ended response. ONE question per turn: call a single ask_user_question, then end your turn — his answer determines the next.

question.description: The single question to ask the learner. ONE question per turn: ask, then end your turn — the answer determines the next question.

details.description: Optional extra context or instructions shown under the question.

label.description: Display label for the answer option — a bare claim, no reasoning

value.description: Optional machine-readable value returned for the option. Defaults to the label.

description.description: Optional extra detail shown below the option

options.description: Optional multiple-choice options. Omit for free-form text input. The learner can always choose 'Other' and type a custom answer when options are provided.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow multiple answers to the same question.

name: plan_init
description: Write or REWRITE this session's plan map — the dependency graph the learner follows live in the plan window. Call once right after the probe concludes, to present the map; re-call whenever the map is wrong (the new block replaces the old tree). A mermaid graph block (any direction): one node per line (`slug[Short Title]` — slugs are permanent lowercase ids: a-z, 0-9, hyphens/underscores), `-->` edges meaning 'from must be understood before to' (chains fine). 5–15 nodes: a map, not a syllabus — one reasoning step per node, compress. Every check you fire names the node it assesses via `nodeId`; where the lesson stands derives from those tags.

mermaid.description:
A mermaid graph block (any direction), e.g.:
graph TD
  primitives[Number primitives] --> operators[Arithmetic operators] --> expressions[Evaluating expressions]
The only strict rule: ids are permanent lowercase slugs (a-z, 0-9, hyphens/underscores) — checks reference them via nodeId. Titles are free single-line text; `-->` means 'from = prerequisite' (chains fine); no subgraphs, styles, or classes.
